review.assessment: Three new invite handlers were added (api.py, bulk_csv.py, sso.py) with identical implementations that call team.add_member() for every email without checking seat availability. The task states the seat limit is enforced on only one of four paths; these three additions contain zero enforcement logic and leave the system at three out of four paths (or four out of four if a fourth handler exists elsewhere) lacking any checks.

findings.actual: No seat count check before team.add_member()
findings.call: python -c "from invites import api; class FakeTeam: add_member=lambda self,e:None; api.invite(FakeTeam(), ['a@b.com'])"
findings.defect: All three invite handlers accept emails without checking whether adding members would exceed seat_limit.
findings.expected: Each handler should reject or defer invitations when the team has reached its seat_limit, e.g. by comparing len(team.members) + len(emails) against team.seat_limit before calling add_member().

findings.actual: Acceptance tests pass while invite paths lack enforcement
findings.defect: The acceptance suite (6 passed) does not appear to cover seat-limit enforcement on the new invite paths, so a bug that allows unlimited members can go undetected.
findings.expected: Tests should verify that inviting more than seat_limit total members fails or is capped.
